dataset_info.name: MORPHE Evaluation Benchmark V3
dataset_info.description: 68-record technical dataset across 7 modules with 16 frozen benchmark queries. All expected_record_ids semantically verified.
dataset_info.source: Hand-authored technical CS/ML knowledge records, MORPHE project benchmark suite

modules.name: Mixed Core Topics (Overloaded)
modules.description: Overcrowded module combining Java OOP and Linear Algebra — intentionally overloaded to trigger SPLIT.

records.text: Java supports object-oriented principles including encapsulation, inheritance, and polymorphism through class hierarchies.
Java classes can implement multiple interfaces but extend only one abstract superclass, enabling flexible type contracts.
Method overriding in Java allows a subclass to define a specialized version of an inherited method via runtime dispatch.
Java garbage collector automatically deallocates heap memory occupied by unreferenced objects using generational collection.
Abstract classes in Java cannot be instantiated directly and define common contracts enforced on all concrete subclasses.
Java Generics provide compile-time type safety by allowing classes and methods to operate on parameterized types.
Java interfaces support default method implementations since Java 8, enabling backwards-compatible API evolution without breaking existing code.
Java heap memory is partitioned into Young and Old Generation regions, with minor GC cycles targeting short-lived objects.
Eigenvalues and eigenvectors characterize invariant directional vectors under linear matrix transformations, fundamental to PCA and spectral decomposition.
Singular Value Decomposition factors any real matrix into left-singular, singular values, and right-singular matrices for low-rank approximation.
The inner dot product computes vector projection and normalizes to cosine similarity in high-dimensional metric spaces.
Matrix multiplication is associative and distributes over addition but is strictly non-commutative in general rectangular cases.
Principal Component Analysis projects high-dimensional data onto orthogonal principal axes that maximize explained variance.
Matrix determinants quantify the signed scaling factor of a linear transformation on the volume spanned by its column vectors.

modules.name: Vector Index Structures
modules.description: Approximate nearest neighbor algorithms and vector index structures for large-scale similarity search.

records.text: FAISS provides fast approximate nearest neighbor search using inverted file index and product quantization techniques.
Hierarchical Navigable Small World graphs (HNSW) offer logarithmic time complexity for dense vector similarity retrieval.
Cosine distance and Euclidean L2 distance are the standard metrics for comparing dense vector embeddings in semantic search.
Vector databases index high-dimensional embeddings generated by transformer encoder models for semantic retrieval.
Inverted file index with flat quantization partitions vector space into Voronoi cells to accelerate approximate nearest neighbor search.
HNSW builds a multi-layer proximity graph where upper layers provide coarse navigation and lower layers enable precise nearest neighbor search.
Annoy uses random projection trees to partition vector space for memory-efficient approximate nearest neighbor similarity search.

modules.name: Dense Embedding Search
modules.description: Dense embedding retrieval systems and vector comparison techniques — near-duplicate of Vector Index Structures to trigger MERGE.

records.text: Dense vector retrieval systems utilize approximate nearest neighbor algorithms to compare query embeddings against stored document vectors.
HNSW index structures enable scalable semantic search across millions of dense embedding vectors in sub-linear query time.
Product Quantization compresses dense vector representations by encoding subvectors into codebook centroids, reducing memory in large-scale search.
Dense vector retrieval compares high-dimensional semantic vectors using cosine similarity and angular distance thresholds for ranking.
Vector similarity search engines query dense embedding vectors generated by sentence encoder neural models against indexed corpora.
Re-ranking pipelines apply cross-encoder models on top of bi-encoder ANN retrieval to improve precision on the final result set.
Bi-encoder models independently encode query and document into fixed-length vectors enabling precomputed offline indexing for fast retrieval.

modules.name: Python Data Engineering
modules.description: Python data processing tools including NumPy, Pandas, and Polars for numerical and tabular data workflows.

records.text: NumPy provides ndarray objects for efficient multi-dimensional vector and matrix computations in Python with C-speed performance.
Pandas DataFrames support tabular data manipulation including filtering, aggregation, groupby, merge, and time-series resampling.
Polars is an ultra-fast columnar DataFrame library implemented in Rust with a Python API, outperforming Pandas on large datasets.
Vectorized operations in NumPy eliminate explicit Python loops, providing substantial performance acceleration for array computations.
NumPy universal functions (ufuncs) apply element-wise mathematical operations across arrays with broadcasting rules for shape compatibility.
Pandas read_csv and to_parquet functions handle columnar data ingestion and serialization for efficient DataFrame storage and retrieval.
Pandas groupby with aggregate functions like sum, mean, and count enables split-apply-combine analytics on tabular datasets.
NumPy linalg module provides linear algebra routines including matrix inversion, least-squares solvers, and eigenvalue decomposition.

modules.name: Machine Learning Pipelines
modules.description: PyTorch deep learning model architectures, training loops, optimization routines, and data loading.

records.text: PyTorch tensors support automatic differentiation via autograd for gradient-based neural network training and optimization.
Cross-entropy loss measures the discrepancy between predicted probability distributions and true categorical labels in classification.
Adam optimizer dynamically adapts per-parameter learning rates using first and second momentum estimates of gradient history.
PyTorch DataLoaders handle batching, shuffling, and multi-threaded data prefetching from datasets for efficient model training.
Backpropagation computes the gradient of the loss function with respect to all model parameters via reverse-mode automatic differentiation.
Dropout regularization randomly deactivates a fraction of neural connections during training to prevent overfitting on small datasets.
Learning rate schedulers in PyTorch dynamically reduce the step size during training to stabilize convergence near loss minima.
Batch normalization standardizes intermediate layer activations during training to reduce internal covariate shift and accelerate convergence.

modules.name: Relational Databases and SQL
modules.description: Relational database concepts, schema normalization, ACID transactions, indexing, and query optimization.

records.text: Relational databases enforce ACID guarantees: Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, and Durability for reliable transaction processing.
B-Tree indexes provide logarithmic time complexity for equality and range query lookups in relational database tables.
Database normalization organizes schema tables into normal forms to minimize data redundancy and eliminate update anomalies.
SQL JOIN operations combine rows from two or more tables based on related key columns to query across relationships.
Foreign key constraints preserve referential integrity between child and parent tables by preventing orphaned records in SQL schemas.
Write-Ahead Logging ensures committed database transactions can be fully recovered after power failures or unexpected crashes.
PostgreSQL query execution plans show whether the optimizer uses sequential scan, index scan, or bitmap scan for each relation.
Connection pooling via PgBouncer reduces overhead of establishing new PostgreSQL connections under high concurrency workloads.

modules.name: Distributed Systems
modules.description: Distributed systems fundamentals: consensus algorithms, replication, partitioning, and fault tolerance.

records.text: The CAP theorem states a distributed data store can guarantee at most two of Consistency, Availability, and Partition tolerance simultaneously.
Raft consensus algorithm selects a leader node to manage replicated log state machines across distributed cluster nodes via heartbeat.
Consistent hashing minimizes key remapping when distributed cache nodes are dynamically added or removed from the ring.
Two-Phase Commit coordinates atomic transaction commits across autonomous distributed database nodes with a prepare-then-commit protocol.
Gossip protocols disseminate membership and state changes across large peer-to-peer networks with eventual consistency guarantees.
Vector clocks track causality and detect concurrent conflicting updates in distributed key-value storage systems across replicas.
Paxos is a consensus protocol that guarantees agreement among a quorum of distributed nodes despite minority node failures.
Eventual consistency allows distributed replicas to temporarily diverge and converge asynchronously, prioritizing availability over immediate consistency.
